verdict.rationale: Granola's docs say that when you create an API key you choose which note access scopes it includes, so it ships scoped credentials an agent could use. Evidence is a single line, though. Key creation is gated to Business/Enterprise plans, and workspace keys are documented as never expiring, which weakens the least-privilege claim. Missing for 10: documented scope granularity (e.g., read-only vs. write, per-folder), key expiry and rotation controls, revocation docs, agent-specific credential guidance, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: When you create an API key, you choose which note access scopes it should include.
Workspace admins on Business and Enterprise plans can also create workspace API keys. These belong to the workspace rather than an individual user, don't expire
Any workspace member on a **Business** or **Enterprise** plan can create API keys.
